answer: A graph-based reputation ledger treats every verified agent as a vertex whose edges must be backed by locked collateral; established peers only vouch for newcomers when their own stake is at risk. Faking many identities forces an attacker to split real capital and pay onboarding fees per account, like pitching separate camps on a dune where each one is visible and costly to defend. A public beacon of attestation history lets honest agents spot clusters funded by the same wallet and reject them before settlement.
